Braised Baby Onions

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 6Prep 20 minCook 45 min

The Feast of the Holy Innocents, often observed with solemn reflection, also traditionally included special meals. These Braised Baby Onions, tender and subtly sweet, offer a comforting and symbolic side dish for a Childermas banquet. Their small size can evoke the innocence commemorated on this day, providing a gentle counterpoint to richer holiday fare.

Ingredients

  • 1.5 pounds (680g) baby onions (such as pearl onions, cipollini, or small shallots), peeled
  • 2 tablespoons (30g) unsalted butter
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) olive oil
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 sprig fresh thyme
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) dry white wine or dry sherry (optional)
  • 1 cup (240ml) vegetable or chicken broth
  • 1 teaspoon sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
  • Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish (optional)

Method

  1. If using pearl onions, blanch them in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then plunge into ice water. Trim the root end and easily slip off the skins. For cipollini or small shallots, simply peel.
  2. In a large skillet or Dutch oven, melt the butter with the olive oil over medium heat. Add the peeled baby onions and sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned on all sides.
  3. Add the minced garlic, thyme sprig, and bay leaf to the skillet. Cook for another minute until fragrant.
  4. Pour in the white wine (if using) and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
  5. Add the broth, sugar, salt, and pepper. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.
  6. Reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and braise for 20-30 minutes, or until the onions are very tender when pierced with a knife.
  7. Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the liquid to reduce and thicken into a glaze that coats the onions.
  8. Remove the thyme sprig and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve warm, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

Tips

  • For a richer, slightly tangy flavor, add a splash of balsamic vinegar during the last few minutes of cooking.
  • These onions can be prepared a day ahead and gently reheated on the stovetop with a little extra broth or water.
  • Ensure you use vegetable broth for a vegetarian or vegan version of this dish.
